Meridian prototype · reconciliation report ·

An actuarial projection engine that reconciles to the cent

Meridian is a prototype alternative to Prophet-style modelling: actuaries write variables as formulas in Python, and a Rust engine projects them across policies, scenarios and months. To test it against something independent, two published open-source models from lifelib were rebuilt in Meridian and checked policy by policy against lifelib's own results. A third model, South African family funeral cover valued on a SAM-style basis, shows the kind of business this is for.

Designed and written by an AI assistant (Claude), directed by one actuary. Every number on this page comes from a run of the code.

Meridian lifelib (reference)

Model 1 · lifelib BasicTerm

Term assurance, 10,000 policies

Monthly projection over 20 years with select-and-ultimate mortality (attained age × duration, five-year select period), duration-based lapses, inflating expenses and first-year commission. The premium is 150% of the net premium, so the model runs twice: once to price, once to project.

Portfolio cash flows by month

Model 2 · lifelib CashValue_ME

Stochastic savings, 10 scenarios at once

A universal-life style product with an account value: single and level premiums, premium loadings, a monthly fee, cost of insurance on the net amount at risk, death benefit of the greater of sum assured and account value, surrender charges by product and duration, whole life to age 115, and lognormal fund returns. lifelib runs one scenario per call; Meridian runs all ten in one pass. A second set turns 1,000 policies into in-force business, with durations and account values, to test the existing-business logic as well.

Portfolio PV of net cash flow, by scenario

Each lifelib dot sits inside its Meridian ring. The values agree to four decimal places on numbers of about 50 billion.

100 generated scenarios

Model 3 · South African family funeral · illustrative SAM basis

One policy, up to eight lives

Each policy covers a main member, a spouse, up to four children and up to two extended-family members, each with their own cover and premium. The policy stays in force until it lapses or the main member dies. Other deaths pay that life's cover and stop its premium, and children's cover ends at 21. Every life is a lane of the engine and the eight lanes of a policy form one group: sum_lives carries the main member's mortality to every life of the policy, the job array variables do in Prophet. The valuation runs a base and six SAM-style stress bases, then aggregates the SCR and adds a cost-of-capital risk margin.

Checks

Run time

Seconds, not minutes

lifelib is written for clarity rather than production speed, so these timings show how much headroom a compiled engine has, not a contest. Measured on one desktop: , best of three runs.

Interrogate the model

Explain any number

Pick a policy, a month and a variable. You see its value, its formula, and the value of everything the formula uses at that month. Click any blue name to follow it back. This is the job Prophet's Diagram View does, for every variable including the procedural ones.

For Prophet users

Familiar concepts, different machinery

Meridian keeps the way a Prophet modeller thinks, with variables defined by formulas over time, products, tables, runs and accumulations, and changes what sits underneath.

Scope

What this shows, and what it does not

It shows that a Python modelling language over a compiled engine can reproduce independent published models exactly. That covers stochastic, in-force and account-value mechanics as well as simple term assurance, and it does so fast. The engine's results are bit-for-bit identical whatever the thread count or batch size, and each lifelib comparison is repeatable from the repository.

It does not show a comparison with Prophet itself. No Prophet software, code or documentation was used. The lifelib models are illustrative, not certified regulatory libraries. The funeral model uses invented assumptions: its mortality curve is shaped like South African population mortality but is not an ASSA or SA85-90 table. Its SAM calculation is simplified, with stresses applied to the whole portfolio and the risk margin projected in proportion to policies in force. Nested stochastic runs, goal-seek and the governance features in the product spec are still to build.

Next: nested runs for projected reserves and capital, and goal-seek for premiums.

Reproduce

cd meridian
python -m maturin develop --release     # build the Rust engine into a virtual env
python -m pytest -q                     # reconciliation tests (lifelib, NumPy reference)
python examples/run_lifelib_basicterm.py
python examples/run_lifelib_cashvalue.py --extra-scenarios 100
